band: Abu Dhabi (ADDC/AADC) industrial >1 MW connected load, time-of-use
source: Abu Dhabi regulator (tariff revision effective 1-Jan-2017) via Gulf News
source_dataset: Gulf News: Electricity and water tariff revised in Abu Dhabi
notes: [AE] Large industrial (>1 MW connected load): 36.6 fils/kWh in summer peak hours, 27 fils/kWh otherwise; light industrial 28.6 fils/kWh flat. Peak window assumed 10:00-22:00, 1-Jun..30-Sep (as described in ADDC tariff pages seen only as search-engine extracts; not stated in the article) = 1,464 of 8,760 h. Flat baseload: (1464x36.6 + 7296x27)/8760 = 28.60 fils/kWh = 286.0 AED/MWh / 3.6725 (AED/USD peg) = 77.89 USD/MWh. Regulated all-in tariff excl. 5% VAT (from 2018). ADDC pages for 2018/2023/2025 appear in search indexes with the same 27/36.6 fils rates, but addc.ae blocks automated access (Cloudflare), so later years are not reported. Dubai (DEWA) not verified (site blocked). Large Abu Dhabi industrials (e.g. aluminium) use captive/bilateral supply.

band: Saudi Arabia Heavy Consumption Tariff, 1st category, transmission-connected
source: Saudi Cabinet decision via Argaam; Saudi Electricity Company
source_dataset: Argaam 02-Oct-2021: Cabinet approves dividing tariffs for electricity-intensive establishments into 2 categories; SEC Consumption Tariffs page (same values, read Oct-2026); SEC Q3-2025 statements note 1 (applied from 1-Jan-2023)
notes: [SA] Intensive/Heavy Consumption Tariff (Council of Ministers res. 111, Sep-2021; applied from 1-Jan-2023 per SEC Q3-2025 statements). 1st category = activities whose electricity cost is >=20% of operating costs excl. raw materials: 12 halalas/kWh transmission-connected (18 distribution); 2nd category (10-19.9%): 18 / 24. Excl. VAT. Eligibility (SEC page): activity on a committee-set list, annual application, energy-efficiency compliance, annual load factor >=80%. A chlor-alkali plant plausibly meets the cost-share and load-factor tests, but whether chlor-alkali is on the eligible-activity list was NOT verified. Eligible customers are not subject to the May-2025 2-halala add-on. 12 halalas = 32.00 USD/MWh at 3.75 SAR/USD. SEC page: https://www.se.com.sa/en/Ourservices/ColumnC/Bills-and-Consumption/ConsumptionTariffs/

band: HV large industry Tamil Nadu HT I-A / HT I (50 MVA, LF 90%)
source: CEA Electricity Tariff & Duty and Average Rates of Electricity Supply in India (annual)
source_dataset: Computed representative bill (TANGEDCO HT I-A; renamed HT I from 10.09.2022)
notes: PERIOD CONVENTION: period = Indian fiscal year start (FY2018-19 = Apr 2018-Mar 2019), not calendar year. Rs/kWh: demand 0.5919 + energy 6.3500 + TOD 0.2249 + electricity tax 0.3583 (5% HT industry, CEA duty tables, w.e.f. 16.06.2003; applied to demand+energy+TOD as CEA does). HT I-A 350 Rs/kVA/month + 635 p/kWh (TN tariff w.e.f. 11.08.2017, CEA March 2019 ed.). TOD for flat load: rule w.e.f. 11.08.2017 (CEA March 2022 ed. TOD summary, HT I-A): peak 06-09 & 18-21h +20% on energy charge, off-peak 22-05h -5% => x1.0354; rule w.e.f. 10.09.2022 (CEA 2023/2024 eds.): peak 06-10 & 18-22h +25%, off-peak 22-05h -5% => x1.0688. Assumptions: billing demand 50,000 kVA, PF 0.90, LF 90% (355 GWh/yr), flat load, supply voltage not differentiated in TN HT I tariff. No fuel/power-purchase surcharge found for TN HT in the CEA books for these years (not separately verified). Excluded: cross-subsidy/additional surcharge (open access only), PF incentives/penalties, any TN tax exemptions. Cross-check: CEA Table 7(h) 50 MW/60% LF/33 kV gives TN 815+41=855 p/kWh (2023 ed.) and excludes TOD. Caveat: TN chlor-alkali producers may rely partly on captive/group-captive or open-access power (JMK Research Aug 2025, https://jmkresearch.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Green-Power-Procurement-in-the-Bulk-Chemical-sector-JMK-Research-2.pdf).
